speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your bleeding issue, can you tell me if you have a family history of bleeding disorders or prolonged bleeding after other surgeries? Also, have you noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding from your gums or nose recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your uncle's history of joint swelling, I suspect a coagulation factor deficiency. To differentiate between Hemophilia A and B, I will order specific clotting assays. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_level, Factor_IX_level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, this points towards a platelet function disorder rather than a coagulation factor deficiency. Do you experience frequent nosebleeds or bleeding from your gums spontaneously, and do you have a personal history of menorrhagia if applicable, or easy bruising after minor trauma? REQUEST TEST: Platelet_aggregation_study, Bleeding_time

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_aggregation_study: Normal aggregation with ristocetin, ADP, epinephrine, and collagen. Bleeding_time: 6 min

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelet aggregation and a mildly prolonged bleeding time, the clinical picture of mucocutaneous bleeding and a family history of joint swelling is highly suggestive of von Willebrand Disease. REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_factor_antigen, von_Willebrand_factor_activity

speaker: Doctor
text: The low von Willebrand factor antigen and activity confirm the diagnosis of von Willebrand Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: von Willebrand Disease
